title: Extract payment policy behind a module boundary
requirement: Move the payment_known, payment_fee, payment_reference and authorization policy from checkout into a new payments module. That module owns those three named helpers and authorize, along with its own authorization data/error contract; it must not depend on checkout, inventory, pricing, shipping, catalog, app, reservations or refunds. Keep checkout.authorize and checkout.Authorization/checkout.Error working as compatibility adapters for callers. checkout.authorize must call payments.authorize; checkout must no longer define the three payment_* helpers. Preserve all HTTP responses, fee/reference behavior, public APIs and tests. Do not merely add an unused module or re-export the old implementation. The functional and structural outcomes are scored separately.
scope: One independent change to the supplied baseline; implement and verify without a human review gate.
acceptance: Behavior is checked through HTTP against the task and unchanged baseline contracts. Payment-boundary additionally has an explicit structural check. Add or update meaningful public tests.
limits: Do not change compiler, vendored guide, AGENTS.md, task.json or this task specification. Use the allowed tool protocol; analysis tools are optional only in the analysis condition.
